title: Policy-as-code engine + automated remediation for residency & retention drift
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a policy-as-code enforcement pipeline and automated configuration drift detection/remediation for data residency and retention settings across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Context: Customers in regulated industries require proof that data never leaves approved jurisdictions, retention windows are enforced, and audit evidence is generated automatically. Current gaps: (1) manual checks during onboarding and upgrades, (2) slow detection of config drift in Private/VPC fleets, (3) lack of machine-readable evidence to attach to compliance reports.

Scope:
- Policy-as-code library (Rego/OPA compatible) for residency and retention rules.
- Continuous scanner that snapshots runtime config (RBAC, storage regions, retention TTLs) and evaluates policies.
- Automated remediation playbooks for low-risk drifts (e.g., incorrect retention TTL reset to policy-compliant value) and escalations for high-risk drifts (e.g., data egress to disallowed region).
- Evidence bundling: signed attestation artifacts, change events, and remediation logs suitable for audit exports.
- Integration points: Console (alerts & remediation UI), Optimize (recommendations), and Private agent (local scanner for air-gapped installs).

Non-goals: Full policy authoring UI (we will expose a CLI + YAML bundles and reference Confluence policy templates for v1).

Constraints & risks:
- Automatic remediation must be opt-in per customer; ensure clear audit trail and reversible actions.
- Private/on-prem deployments cannot call our hosted control plane for enforcement; need signed policies and a local enforcement agent.
- Latency: drift scanner should be low-overhead and default to sampling frequency to avoid perf regressions on control-plane databases.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff: scoped core acceptance criteria and identified OPA/Rego for policy language. Maya to draft policy templates for residency and retention.

2026-03-02 - Architecture sync: decided on hybrid enforcement model: hosted control plane issues signed desired-state bundles; Private agent performs local evaluation and remediation. Action: Arjun to prototype signed bundle format.

2026-03-06 - Trade-off note: full auto-remediation introduces risk for customer workloads. MVP will: auto-fix retention TTLs (reversible) and create block-and-alert for region violations. PM asked to include clear opt-in flag per customer.
2026-03-09 - Design review with Console team: added an Alerts -> Remediation UI flow and a runbook link to Confluence. Design requested ability to preview changes before apply.
2026-03-12 - Security review requested (SR-REQ-1124). Initial answer: require signed change sets, immutable event logs, and a rollback API. Security assigned to review the agent hardening checklist.

2026-03-14 - Prototype: local scanner PoC completed in internal dogfood cluster. Found 12 test tenants with misconfigured TTLs; automated remediation applied successfully for 9 (3 were blocked due to custom retention exemptions). GitHub PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2745
acceptance_criteria: Policy library published with at least 2 example rules: data_residency_allowed_regions and retention_max_days
Continuous scanner can enumerate target configs for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private agent and produce policy evaluation traces
Automated remediation: retention TTL reset action implemented and reversible; remediation audit log entries generated
Evidence bundle format documented and can be exported from Console (JSON + signed manifest), and includes evaluation traces, remediation steps, and provenance
End-to-end test in dogfood: detect drift in Private agent, trigger remediation or escalation, and attach evidence to a draft compliance report
